boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free, under-21-safe study, art, outdoor, and public-history stops on campus and around Bristol.

cards.title: Settle into the University Library
cards.subtitle: RWU Bristol Campus
cards.notes: Bring a study partner, choose a collaborative or individual work area, and check the visitor desk if you are arriving from off campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus study hang with library resources and work space.
cards.evidence_claim: RWU identifies the Main Library’s Learning Commons as providing collaborative and individual study space; visitors may use library facilities and resources.
cards.access_notes: Visitors must sign the visitor log at the Information Desk; RWU users receive priority.

cards.title: Look through ROGER THAT Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Center, RWU Bristol Campus
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition before heading over, then take time to look closely at the student work, archival material, or local art on view.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery dedicated to rotating art and archival displays.
cards.evidence_claim: RWU says ROGER THAT regularly hosts exhibitions of local artists, archival finds, student work, and other curiosities, with programming for students and the public.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities | Roger Williams University
cards.access_notes: Located in the Fine Arts Center; confirm the current exhibition and building access before visiting.

cards.title: Take the RWU 360 virtual tour together
cards.subtitle: Online from Roger Williams University
cards.notes: Open the 360 experience on a shared screen and compare the waterfront, academic buildings, and student spaces before planning an in-person walk.
cards.short_summary: A no-travel way to explore the Bristol campus with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: RWU offers a 360 virtual-tour experience for navigating academic buildings, student amenities, and campus landmarks from home.
cards.source_title: Visit Campus, Tour In-Person or Virtual | Roger Williams University
cards.access_notes: Online activity; use the university’s “Launch Experience” link.

cards.entity_name: RWU Shell Path and Sailing Center Observation Deck
cards.title: Walk the shell path to the observation deck
cards.subtitle: RWU Bristol Campus waterfront
cards.notes: Meet in daylight, follow the shell path toward the Sailing Center, and pause at the observation deck for Mount Hope Bay views.
cards.short_summary: A simple waterfront campus walk ending at the Sailing Center deck.
cards.evidence_claim: RWU invites campus visitors to walk the shell path and relax on the observation deck at the Sailing Center.
cards.source_title: Visit Campus, Tour In-Person or Virtual | Roger Williams University
cards.access_notes: Stay on designated paths and follow campus access guidance.

cards.title: Use the library’s public Wi-Fi
cards.subtitle: 525 Hope Street, Bristol
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or phone, connect to Bristol Public, and use the building or backyard as a low-key place to read, work, or catch up.
cards.short_summary: A public-library study stop with free, password-free Wi-Fi.
cards.evidence_claim: Rogers Free Library states that public Wi-Fi is free 24 hours a day, seven days a week and is available throughout the building and backyard.
cards.access_notes: The Wi-Fi is public and password-free; the library’s building hours are posted separately.

cards.entity_name: Rogers Free Library Local Use Card
cards.title: Sign up for a local-use library card
cards.subtitle: Rogers Free Library, 525 Hope Street
cards.notes: If you meet the eligibility rules, bring the required school or address documentation and ask circulation staff about using Bristol materials at the library.
cards.short_summary: Eligible Bristol-school students can obtain a no-charge local-use card.
cards.evidence_claim: Rogers Free Library’s policy says free local-use cards may be issued to non-Rhode Island residents attending Bristol schools during the school year.
cards.source_title: Local Use Only Library Card Policy | Rogers Free Library
cards.access_notes: Eligibility and documentation apply; card use is limited to the Rogers Free Library location and Bristol materials.

cards.title: Walk the Bristol end of the East Bay Bike Path
cards.subtitle: Independence Park to the Bristol waterfront
cards.notes: Start at Independence Park, walk or roll a short stretch at a comfortable pace, and share the path courteously with cyclists and other users.
cards.short_summary: A state-maintained shared-use path ending at Bristol’s waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: RIDOT identifies the East Bay Bike Path as a 14.5-mile route ending at Independence Park in Bristol and describes it as a recreational and transportation route.
cards.source_title: East Bay Bike Path | Rhode Island Department of Transportation
cards.access_notes: Use the shared path responsibly and check RIDOT notices for detours or construction updates.

cards.title: Take a slow lap through Thomas Park
cards.subtitle: Hope Street, Bristol
cards.notes: Use the winding paths for a short catch-up walk, then pause at a bench or overlook for birdwatching, sketching, or quiet conversation.
cards.short_summary: A passive park with native plantings, paths, and overlooks.
cards.evidence_claim: Explore Bristol describes Thomas Park as a 5.1-acre passive naturalistic park with native plantings, walking paths, benches, overlooks, and space for birdwatching, painting, or photography.
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight and respect planted areas and wildlife.

cards.title: Explore Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.subtitle: 282 North Main Street, Providence
cards.notes: Make it a daytime outing: walk the memorial grounds, read the interpretation, and pair it with a conversation about the history presented on site.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission National Park Service historic site in Providence.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that no entrance pass is required and there is no fee to enter Roger Williams National Memorial.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes | Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.access_notes: No entrance fee or entrance pass is required; transportation to Providence is separate.

cards.title: Follow a public shoreline-access route
cards.subtitle: Public access rights-of-way along the East Bay Bike Path, Bristol
cards.notes: Use the state’s shoreline-access guidance, stay on public rights-of-way, and make a short daylight walk focused on the waterfront rather than private property.
cards.short_summary: A self-directed walk connecting Bristol’s documented public shoreline access points.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhode Island’s Coastal Resources Management Council documented a Bristol shoreline tour using four public access rights-of-way along the East Bay Bike Path and described the event as free.
cards.source_title: Bristol Shoreline Access Walking Tour | Rhode Island Coastal Resources Management Council
cards.access_notes: The cited guided event was historical; use only clearly marked public access points and do not enter private property.
